_about: Historical records per site, keyed by site id from sites.json. Records cite either 'pages' (printed page numbers in the source; images live at {source.pagesDir}/p{page}.jpg) or a web 'url'. 'siteMatch' records whether the link between the old record and the modern site is verified or assumed. Full citations and verification notes: sources/duxbury-town-records-1642-1770/FINDINGS.md and sources/town-landing-report-1975/FINDINGS.md

etheridge-1893.title: Copy of the Old Records of the Town of Duxbury, Mass., from 1642 to 1770
etheridge-1893.detail: Transcribed 1892 by George Etheridge; printed Plymouth: Avery & Doten, 1893. Secondary source (transcription of the original manuscript books).

nsrwa-shipyard.title: North and South Rivers Watershed Association: Shipyard Lane Beach listing
nsrwa-shipyard.detail: Web listing (checked 2026-11-09). Reports the wording of the plaque on site and the town ownership.

drew-ellison-grace.title: Drew Archives: Grace Ellison Letter (DAL.SMS.360), finding aid
drew-ellison-grace.detail: Duxbury Rural & Historical Society archives (checked 2026-11-09). Ellison family background; does not mention Shipyard Lane.

tlsc-1975.title: Report of the Duxbury Town Landing Study Committee, 1975
tlsc-1975.detail: Typescript report to the Selectmen by Donald F. Corcoran, Robert Cooper and Robert S. Ramsay, appointed under Article 65 of the 1974 annual town meeting. It includes typed transcriptions of town report excerpts from 1894 to 1972. Those transcriptions are a secondary source, so check each one against the original Town Report. The page links go to pages of the scanned copy (scan page numbers, not the report's typed page numbers).

10.title: Committee on Town Landings: the Mattakeeset Court landing is "of no practical value in its present condition"
10.quote: The "Town Landing" at Mattakeesett Court is of no practical value in its present condition. It should be properly laid out.
10.by: Report of Committee on Town Landings, Town Report 1908 p. 43 (Alfred E. Green, Chairman)

10.title: Land exchange with Wallace C. Flagg gives the town 100 more feet of frontage; deeds passed by 1917
10.quote: agreement has been made with Mr. Wallace C. Flagg for an exchange of land on Mattakeeset Court giving the Town one hundred (100) feet more frontage on the Court.
10.by: Selectmen's Reports 1916 and 1917 p. 5; Town Meeting March 11, 1916 p. 88 ($400 appropriated). Deed book and page not given

10.title: $150 for a landing and bathing beach; sea wall and entrance to the shore completed
10.quote: Mattakeeset Court Town Landing Sea Wall and entrance to shore have been completed for amount appropriated.

10.title: 1975 committee: post ramp rules and a 24-hour parking limit; realign the parking
10.quote: Some users park for 2-3 days at a time while off for the weekend. Such use is unfair to other users.

11.title: Public bathing at Winsor Street is challenged; the Selectmen begin establishing a town landing there
11.quote: it is exemplified in the case of Winsor street, where the right of public bathing has been brought into question.
11.by: Report of Committee on Town Landings, Town Report 1908 p. 43

11.title: Votes on widening the east end of Winsor Street (left to the Selectmen in 1919; tabled 1922)
11.quote: Voted That the matter of widening the Easterly end of Winsor Street be left in the hands of the Selectmen.
11.by: Town Meeting March 8, 1919, Art. 21 (Town Report p. 78); 1920 p. 79; 1921 p. 5; 1922 Art. 38

11.title: 1975 committee: clear brush and restore "this nearly abandoned town landing"
11.quote: Rough brush should be cut back and an opening be made to enable the addition of a few loads of sand and gravel to be brought in to restore this nearly abandoned town landing.

12.title: Town accepts Water Street and its extension to the shore; Charles C. Clapp gives the land
12.quote: This recommendation is made with the approval of Mr. Charles C. Clapp, who kindly gives the land for the purpose, simply asking in return that a sidewalk be constructed
12.by: Report on Town Landings 1900; votes 1899 (highway near James K. Burgess house, "providing there is no land damage") and 1901 p. 7 (extension accepted). Town Clerk Plan Book 2 p. 113

12.title: 1975 committee: fix culvert and erosion; no parking
12.quote: This site has not enough turning area and for reasons of security and safety we recommend that it be posted for "No Parking."

13.title: Town accepts Josselyn Avenue as a highway over land of John E. Josselyn
13.quote: Voted To accept Highway as laid out by the Selectmen February 11, 1907, commencing at South Station Street and running Easterly over land of John E. Josselyn
13.by: Town Meeting March 4, 1907 (Town Report pp. 52–53). The 1975 committee lists "Josselyn Avenue" as a town landing

13.title: 1975 committee: reopen the foot passage for foot and bicycle use only
13.quote: Recommend reopening of a foot passageway and posting for "Foot and Bicycle Use Only."

14.title: Town names the street to the town landing "Hardin Hill Road"
14.quote: Voted To name the street on the Southerly side of Washington Street beginning at the West Boundary of land of St. Margaret's and following to the Town Landing "Hardin Hill Road".
14.by: Town Meeting March 1, 1941, Art. 32 (Town Report p. 136). Plan: Town of Duxbury Plan Book 1 p. 17

14.title: Town accepts a change in the layout of the way from Washington Street through land of the Sisters of St. Margaret
14.quote: Voted, To accept the change made in the layout of the way From Washington Street through land now owned by the Sisters Saint Margaret and formerly Baldwin
14.by: Town Report for the year ending Jan 1, 1904, p. 58. That this is the way to Hardin Hill landing is assumed from the 1941 naming vote

14.title: 1975 committee: limited parking, drainage, and first refusal on the neighboring land
14.quote: We recommend acquisition of the right of first refusal by the town of all adjacent properties as future park and recreational areas.

15.title: Town accepts "the road and landing near Allen's Wharf" as laid out by the Selectmen
15.quote: Voted to accept the road and landing near Allen's Wharf, so-called, as laid out by the Selectmen.
15.by: Town Report 1896, Report of Town Clerk p. 49, Art. 10 (warrant 1895 p. 44). The 1975 committee identifies this as Howland's Lane. Plan: Town of Duxbury Plan Book 1 p. 16. NOTE: NSRWA says the town bought the land in 1894; not reconciled

15.title: $150 for repairs to the road to the town landing near Allen's Wharf at Captain's Hill
15.quote: Voted To appropriate one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00) for repairs of the road leading to the Town Landing near Allen's Wharf at Captain's Hill.

15.title: Town names the street from Crescent Street to the shore "Howlands Lane"
15.quote: Voted unanimously to name the street leading from Crescent Street to the Shore Howlands Lane.

15.title: 1975 committee: "a prime site for further development"; the town should get first refusal on Blairhaven
15.quote: In the event that the New Church Union Headquarters at Newbury Street, Boston, ever decides to dispose of the property (or any part thereof) known as Blairhaven, we recommend that the Town of Duxbury should acquire the right of first refusal
15.by: 1975 Town Landing Study Committee, recommendation 13 (see also Article 103, 1975 Town Warrant)

16.title: Committee recommends a landing through the Foote and Crosby property on the east side of Border Street
16.quote: recommend that a public town landing be established through property owned by the Foote's and the Crosby's
16.by: Report on Town Landings, Town Report 1906 p. 39 (A. E. Green, C. F. Allen, J. H. Glover). The 1975 committee files this under Landing Road

16.title: Town votes to lay out a landing "through the property of Mrs. Foote" and appropriates $500
16.quote: Voted That the Selectmen lay out a Town Landing at "Hicks Point" so-called, and another through the property of Mrs. Foote.
16.by: Town Meeting March 8, 1909 (Town Report p. 64). Town of Duxbury Plan Book 2 p. 148: "Town Landing Landing Road, 9/12/09"

16.title: 1975 committee: foot and bicycle landing, parking for three cars
16.quote: Recommend posting as a foot and bicycle landing.

17.title: Committee recommends a landing through land of Harrison Loring, "known as Hick's Point"
17.quote: another through land owned by Mr. Harrison Loring, known as Hick's Point, both being on the easterly side of Border street
17.by: Report on Town Landings, Town Report 1906 p. 39 (A. E. Green, C. F. Allen, J. H. Glover)

17.title: Town votes that the Selectmen lay out a landing at Hicks Point and appropriates $500
17.quote: Voted That the Selectmen lay out a Town Landing at "Hicks Point" so-called, and another through the property of Mrs. Foote.
17.by: Town Meeting March 8, 1909 (Town Report p. 64). The 1908 report notes the Legislature, at Duxbury's initiative, authorized towns to lay out highways to low water mark

17.title: 1975 committee: foot and bicycle landing, parking for three cars and two trailers
17.quote: We feel minor improvement of road and ramp with gravel and natural materials to give limited small boat with trailer access for hunters and users of the marsh.
17.by: 1975 Town Landing Study Committee, recommendation 15. Its 1975 photos show a marker here

WW-06.title: Captain's Nook highway (30 ft) and a cart way down to the Bay through the Standish farm
WW-06.quote: a convenient cart way is allowed down to the Bay through the farm of said Standish, which is also allowed by said Standish's consent
WW-06.by: Selectmen Edward Southworth, John Simons, John Partridge

WW-06.title: Captain's Nook highway re-laid with compass bearings; way through Capt. Wait Wadsworth's land down to the salt bay
WW-06.quote: there is a way through Capt. Wait Wadsworth's land, down to the salt bay, where it may be the most beneficial and least prejudicial to each other, forever
WW-06.by: Selectmen Ezra Arnold, John Wadsworth; accepted at Town Meeting

WW-06.title: Town accepts the homesite of Myles Standish from the Standish Monument Association
WW-06.quote: Voted unanimously that the Town accept the homesite of Myles Standish, at Standish Shore, and send thanks to the Trustees of the Standish Monument Association.
WW-06.by: Town Meeting March 1, 1930, Art. 15 (Town Report p. 81). Plan: Town of Duxbury Plan Book 2 p. 144 ("Old Myles Standish Homestead including Shore Way to water")

WW-06.title: 1975 committee: the Shore Way "currently qualifies as a landing"
WW-06.quote: posting as a foot and bicycle landing after this way is designated a landing by the Selectpersons (as it currently qualifies as a landing).
WW-06.by: 1975 Town Landing Study Committee, recommendation II.3

09.title: Old landing place laid out as a common town landing; 40 ft highway to the Marshfield–Plymouth road
09.quote: allowing all the ground on the Southerly side of the said fence to bluefish river channel, for a common landing place for said town
09.by: Selectmen Edward Southworth, John Simons Sen., John Partridge; recorded by John Wadsworth, Town Clerk

09.title: Town meeting: Abraham Samson may gate the highway, and grants the town the landing privilege forever
09.quote: the benefit and privilege of the said landing place for the landing and carrying away their hay &c forever

09.title: Town meeting: Joseph Drew and partners allowed to build a dam and gristmill on Bluefish River
09.quote: The town gave liberty to Joseph Drew and his partners to build a dam and Gristmill on Blue fish river

09.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 6; the town adopts the surveyed landings and records the plans at Plymouth (Registry Plan Book 2, p. 6)
09.quote: At Mill pond, by Blue Fish river, by town highway adjoining land formerly belonging to Amherst A. Frazer.
09.by: Committee: Laurence Bradford, Hamilton Wadsworth (report dated Jan 21, 1899; Town Report for 1898, p. 38). Adopted at Town Meeting March 6, 1899: "the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office". The committee believed it the oldest landing in town, "first defined in 1715". Part was sold to Samuel A. Frazar and others, Dec. 30, 1840 (Plymouth Deeds Book 201, p. 87). NOTE: the 1975 committee files No. 6 under "St. George Street, by Old Mill Pond", which may be a different spot from this site.

09.title: Committee reports the town owns part of the wharf at Blue River Bridge; J. H. Killian offers the rest
09.quote: the town owns a part of the wharf situated at the southeast corner of Blue River Bridge
09.by: Report on Town Landings, Town Report for the year ending Jan 1, 1900 (A. E. Green, L. Bradford, H. Wadsworth)

09.title: Selectmen authorized to move the south line of the town land at Blue Fish River two feet north
09.quote: Voted to authorize the Selectmen to rectify the southerly line of the town land between Blue Fish River and Riverview Avenue, moving the boundary stones two feet northerly.
09.by: Town Meeting March 11, 1916, Town Report 1916 p. 90

09.title: 1975 committee: "Old Mill" as a small-craft launch with an 8-car, 3-trailer lot
09.quote: Recommended as a down river site for launching small craft; i.e. prams, canoes, skiffs, etc., and posting as such.

06.title: Selectmen to lay out the way into Powder Point; gate allowed only if a good cart way is kept open
06.quote: provided the said Alden gives or allows a good cart way through his way as is usual, into Powder Point

06.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 1; the town adopts the surveyed landings and records the plans at Plymouth (Registry Plan Book 2, p. 6)
06.quote: At Powder Point End by new bridge.
06.by: Committee: Laurence Bradford, Hamilton Wadsworth (report dated Jan 21, 1899; Town Report for 1898, p. 38). Adopted at Town Meeting March 6, 1899: "the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office". The report says No. 1 was "laid out by the County Commissioners in January, 1870"; the 1899 meeting voted it be recorded as a "Highway to the sea."

06.title: 1975 committee: recommendations for both sides of Powder Point Bridge (Powder Point end)
06.quote: The lower parking lot is a part of the actual landing.

07.title: Selectmen to lay out the way into Powder Point; gate allowed only if a good cart way is kept open
07.quote: provided the said Alden gives or allows a good cart way through his way as is usual, into Powder Point

07.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 1; the town adopts the surveyed landings and records the plans at Plymouth (Registry Plan Book 2, p. 6)
07.quote: At Powder Point End by new bridge.
07.by: Committee: Laurence Bradford, Hamilton Wadsworth (report dated Jan 21, 1899; Town Report for 1898, p. 38). Adopted at Town Meeting March 6, 1899: "the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office". The report says No. 1 was "laid out by the County Commissioners in January, 1870"; the 1899 meeting voted it be recorded as a "Highway to the sea."

07.title: 1975 committee: recommendations for both sides of Powder Point Bridge (Powder Point end)
07.quote: The lower parking lot is a part of the actual landing.

WW-01.title: Plaque on site credits Eben Ellison's gift of land and money for the beach
WW-01.quote: whose generous gift of land and money made this beach available for the enjoyment of the citizens of Duxbury
WW-01.by: Plaque text as reported by NSRWA, which lists the owner as the Town of Duxbury. The town accepted the gift in 1944 (see the 1944 record)

WW-01.title: Ellison family background: summer residents of Powder Point and “great benefactors to the town”
WW-01.quote: The Ellison family had long roots in Duxbury and were great benefactors to the town.
WW-01.by: Biographical note: Grace married Eben Howes Ellison in 1893. Whether he is the Eben Ellison on the plaque is assumed

WW-01.title: Town Meeting accepts Eben H. Ellison's deed of the upland and beach, to low water mark, restricted to Duxbury residents and their guests
WW-01.quote: Said premises are conveyed subject to the restriction that they shall be used only for recreational purposes and be restricted to the use of the residents of Duxbury and their guests; and to the further restriction that no pier shall be erected on said premises.
WW-01.by: Annual Town Meeting 1944, Art. 24, voted unanimously (Town Report for 1944 p. 108). The 1943 Selectmen's Report (p. 12) notes "some opposition". The deed's book and page are not given; the 1893 I. L. Rich plan it cites is Registry Plan Book 1 p. 9

01.title: Town accepts the highway from Cut Island to the Hummock at Duxbury Beach and appropriates $500 to build it
01.quote: Voted To accept the Highway from the South End of Cut Island to the North end of Hummock as laid out by the Selectmen
01.by: Town Reports 1897 p. 45 (Art. 9) and 1898 p. 52, under the petition of B. S. Bryant and others. The 1975 committee files this under Ford's Stand; no layout of the landing itself is cited

01.title: 1975 committee: Ford's Stand needs a study of use, parking and security
01.quote: the town may well develop one of the four most important landings here.

02.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 5; the town adopts the surveyed landings and records the plans at Plymouth (Registry Plan Book 2, p. 6)
02.quote: At Old Cove, bordering on land now belonging to Samuel Weston and others, by new town road leading to Abrams Hill
02.by: Committee: Laurence Bradford, Hamilton Wadsworth (report dated Jan 21, 1899; Town Report for 1898, p. 38). Adopted at Town Meeting March 6, 1899: "the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office". The committee called it "the most valuable one that the town possesses" (date on the town books: 1834).

02.title: Deed: Town of Duxbury to George Loring (Plymouth Deeds Book 215, p. 28); part of the landing conveyed, the rest reserved to the town forever
02.quote: it is expressly stated by deed, Dec. 30, 1843 - Plymouth Deeds, book 215, page 28 - Town of Duxbury to George Loring, that the present landing place shall be forever reserved to the town.
02.by: As summarized in the 1899 Report on Town Landings, following the Town Meeting of Nov. 13, 1843. The deed itself has not yet been viewed

02.title: Town votes to exchange land at the Old Cove landing with Helen Ripley Clapp and Clara Ripley Evans
02.quote: Voted To exchange a piece of land at town landing at Old Cove, so-called, for a piece adjoining said town landing
02.by: Town Report 1924, p. 72 (the article was first tabled March 17, 1923)

02.title: 1975 committee: post parking for ten cars, add sand and gravel for a beach, fix the washout
02.quote: This site, with a minimal amount of effort, would be a good high water bathing site for limited local use.

03.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 4; the town adopts the surveyed landings and records the plans at Plymouth (Registry Plan Book 2, p. 6)
03.quote: At Foot of lane through land now belonging to E. F. Adams, near what was formerly Drew's salt works, at Duck Hill river.
03.by: Committee: Laurence Bradford, Hamilton Wadsworth (report dated Jan 21, 1899; Town Report for 1898, p. 38). Adopted at Town Meeting March 6, 1899: "the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office". Date on the town books: 1834.

03.title: Mrs. Ellen F. Adams allowed to move the way to the landing to the east side of her property
03.quote: Voted To grant Mrs. Ellen F. Adams the right to change the way through her property to the landing to run on the easterly side of her property
03.by: Town Report 1904. The 1899 report places this landing on land of "E. F. Adams"; that this vote concerns this landing is assumed

03.title: 1975 committee: post as a foot landing, no parking
03.quote: Recommended that the site be posted as a foot landing. No parking. (Primary use is as an access to the marsh.)

04.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 3; the town adopts the surveyed landings and records the plans at Plymouth (Registry Plan Book 2, p. 6)
04.quote: At Foot of lane through land formerly belonging to Simeon Soule, by Duck Hill river.
04.by: Committee: Laurence Bradford, Hamilton Wadsworth (report dated Jan 21, 1899; Town Report for 1898, p. 38). Adopted at Town Meeting March 6, 1899: "the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office". The committee called it "a very old town landing" (dates on the town books: 1803 and 1834).

04.title: 1975 committee: post as a foot landing, no parking
04.quote: Recommended posting as a foot landing. No parking.
04.by: 1975 Town Landing Study Committee, recommendation 4. Its 1975 photos show a stone marker here

05.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 2; the town adopts the surveyed landings and records the plans at Plymouth (Registry Plan Book 2, p. 6)
05.quote: At Foot of lane by land formerly belonging to Reuben and Clark Peterson, by Duck Hill river.
05.by: Committee: Laurence Bradford, Hamilton Wadsworth (report dated Jan 21, 1899; Town Report for 1898, p. 38). Adopted at Town Meeting March 6, 1899: "the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office". Date on the town books: 1834.

05.title: 1975 committee: foot landing only, keep the emergency access clear
05.quote: Recommended as a foot landing. Parking not recommended. Do not block emergency landing.
05.by: 1975 Town Landing Study Committee, recommendation 5. Its 1975 photos show markers here

WW-02.title: Town accepts the Standish Shore ways (Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit Roads) as laid out by the Selectmen
WW-02.quote: Voted, to accept the ways at Standish Shore, as laid out by the Selectmen February 11, 1907. Columbus Avenue, leading from southwest corner of land of Caroline C. Rushton. Brewster Road, Samoset Road, Sagamore Road and Massasoit Road, all leading from Columbus Avenue to the shore.

WW-02.title: Proposed re-layout of the Porter Shore roads; the original plans are Registry Plan Book 1 p. 227 (1901) and Plan Book 2 p. 290 (1903)
WW-02.quote: This plan shows Puritan Road and the four parallel roads from it to the shore, Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit.
WW-02.by: Town Report for 1920, "Proposed Re-Layout of Porter Shore Roads"

WW-02.title: 1975 committee: these ways have been wrongly posted as private; it asks for a Standish Shore Study Committee
WW-02.quote: some of these ways are or have been incorrectly identified or posted as private. This should cease.
WW-02.by: 1975 Town Landing Study Committee, recommendation II.4. It also says town funds improved these ways to the 1907–08 high water mark

WW-03.title: Town accepts the Standish Shore ways (Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit Roads) as laid out by the Selectmen
WW-03.quote: Voted, to accept the ways at Standish Shore, as laid out by the Selectmen February 11, 1907. Columbus Avenue, leading from southwest corner of land of Caroline C. Rushton. Brewster Road, Samoset Road, Sagamore Road and Massasoit Road, all leading from Columbus Avenue to the shore.

WW-03.by: Town Report for 1920, "Proposed Re-Layout of Porter Shore Roads"

WW-03.title: 1975 committee: these ways have been wrongly posted as private; it asks for a Standish Shore Study Committee
WW-03.quote: some of these ways are or have been incorrectly identified or posted as private. This should cease.
WW-03.by: 1975 Town Landing Study Committee, recommendation II.4. It also says town funds improved these ways to the 1907–08 high water mark

WW-03.title: Town instructs the Selectmen to lay out part of Samoset Road as a public highway
WW-03.quote: Voted that the Town instruct the Selectmen to lay out as a public highway that part of Samoset Road
WW-03.by: Town Meeting March 1, 1941, Art. 36 (Town Report p. 137). It cites the plan "A part of the Old Standish and Elder Brewster Farms" (rev. 1903), Registry Plan Book 2 p. 290. The text says "Samoset", which supports the site's name

WW-04.title: Town accepts the Standish Shore ways (Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit Roads) as laid out by the Selectmen
WW-04.quote: Voted, to accept the ways at Standish Shore, as laid out by the Selectmen February 11, 1907. Columbus Avenue, leading from southwest corner of land of Caroline C. Rushton. Brewster Road, Samoset Road, Sagamore Road and Massasoit Road, all leading from Columbus Avenue to the shore.

WW-04.by: Town Report for 1920, "Proposed Re-Layout of Porter Shore Roads"

WW-04.by: 1975 Town Landing Study Committee, recommendation II.4. It also says town funds improved these ways to the 1907–08 high water mark

WW-05.title: Town accepts the Standish Shore ways (Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit Roads) as laid out by the Selectmen
WW-05.quote: Voted, to accept the ways at Standish Shore, as laid out by the Selectmen February 11, 1907. Columbus Avenue, leading from southwest corner of land of Caroline C. Rushton. Brewster Road, Samoset Road, Sagamore Road and Massasoit Road, all leading from Columbus Avenue to the shore.

WW-05.title: Proposed re-layout of the Porter Shore roads; the original plans are Registry Plan Book 1 p. 227 (1901) and Plan Book 2 p. 290 (1903)
WW-05.quote: This plan shows Puritan Road and the four parallel roads from it to the shore, Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit.

WW-05.quote: some of these ways are or have been incorrectly identified or posted as private. This should cease.
WW-05.by: 1975 Town Landing Study Committee, recommendation II.4. It also says town funds improved these ways to the 1907–08 high water mark

WW-05.title: Selectmen instructed to lay out Massasoit Road and Mayflower Avenue as a public highway to near the Myles Standish cellar
WW-05.quote: Voted To instruct Selectmen to lay out as a public highway, Massasoit Road and Mayflower Avenue from Columbus Avenue to a point near the old Myles Standish cellar.
WW-05.by: Town Meeting March 13, 1920 (Town Report p. 79). By 1921 the Selectmen reported both roads "graded and hardened"

WW-09.title: Town votes to acquire Bay Farm (about 44 acres, Block P) for recreation; $200,000
WW-09.quote: acquire in Fee simple by purchase, or eminent domain, if necessary, for recreational purposes
WW-09.by: Town Meeting 1972, Art. 21, carried 413 to 97. Parcels from the Bay Farm Trust and the Grace M. Walker Trust; Land Court Plan 14792-6

WW-09.title: 1975 committee: a separate group should plan Bay Farm's beach, parking and security
WW-09.quote: We feel to allow this area to continue unattended is to invite misuse and the possible creation of a public nuisance.
WW-09.by: 1975 Town Landing Study Committee, recommendation II.2

WW-10.title: 1975 committee: the town's only documented fresh water way (plan: Town of Duxbury Plan Book 2 p. 111)
WW-10.quote: We recommend that the Town's only documented fresh water way be posted as: A recreational area.
WW-10.by: 1975 Town Landing Study Committee, recommendation II.1. Its reference sheet says "the Town has a public way to the shores"
